correctness.rationale: The low-valuation primitive square-zero matrices over R/(pi^e) form the GL2 conjugacy class of a single Jordan block, of size P_e=(q^2-1)q^(2e-2). For k<ceil(n/2), reduction modulo pi^(n-2k) and q^(4k) lifts yield constant (q^2-1)q^(2n-2) layer; determinant takes every permitted value with equal q^(3k) fiber and Smith forms yield the explicit image-length terms. High valuation cone pi^ceil(n/2) M2(R) is automatically square zero, its full rank-by-determinant valuation census gives final terms. Independent exhaustive matrices over Z/4, Z/8, Z/9 produced histograms (1,9,18), (1,9,30,72), (1,32,120) at image lengths 0..n, matching formulas. Corollary Cent(J_n⊕J_n)=M2(Fq[t]/t^n) correctly identifies Fq-linear square-zero Jordan type (2^r,1^(2n-2r)). Pure ring statement covers all commutative finite chain rings n>=2 incl mixed characteristic, not general local rings or larger matrices.

originality.rationale: Oblak, Britnell–Wildon and Bogdanić et al. study nilpotent commuting-matrix compatible Jordan types, especially for centralizer of two equal blocks. Their prior results are qualitative existence / orbit types, not the exact multiplicity of each square-zero Fq-linear Jordan shape, nor universal finite chain ring image-length distribution. Older Bollman–Ramírez finite ring nilpotent counting and Brawley Drazin index enumeration remain plausible aliases but accessible evidence does not establish domination of this joint refined census.

value.rationale: Exact image-length distribution, valuation equidistribution, and q,n-universality across ramification are natural fine invariants of square-zero matrices. The commuting equal-block centralizer interpretation gives precise multiplicities in a classical classification problem, beyond mere existence of shapes; total and maximal-image counts are meaningful corollaries.
